newsitem.title: USA: Public may learn more about Clinton's health.
newsitem.headline: Public may learn more about Clinton's health.

text.p: The White House said on Friday it was considering releasing more information about President Bill Clinton's health in answer to complaints from Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole.

"The president is in excellent overall health. And it's apparent to us we're going to have to do whatever it takes to satisfy you and the American public that that's true," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.

Dole has repeatedly demanded that Clinton release his full medical records and suggested that his failure to do so means the president may be hiding something. "Let's have your health records, Mr. President," Dole said on Thursday. "I gave them all of mine."

At a news briefing on Thursday during a Clinton campaign trip in Fresno, California, McCurry was asked bluntly whether the president had a sexually transmitted disease. McCurry denied that was so and told reporters he was "astonished" the question had been raised. The topic consumed about five minutes of the news briefing.

At Friday's news briefing at the White House, the topic of Clinton's medical records came up again. McCurry replied that officials were looking for ways to release more information. Asked when they might do so, he said, "Stay tuned."

Each time Clinton has had an annual physical while in office, the White House has released many details of his health, such as his weight, blood cholesterol level and blood pressure, as well as the fact that a number of precancerous growths, the result of overexposure to the sun, have been removed from his face.

White House and Clinton campaign officials have accused Dole of grasping at straws to try to cut into the president's large lead in public opinion polls less than two months before the Nov. 5 election.
